note: Re-issue of r2026-11-10-profile-small, which is spent and useless: it ran the ENTRY named small and profiled the large network. Its own output says so twice - `model:  /opt/neuralscreen/model` as the second line, and `entry port-profile-small - env from policy: NS_WORKER_CMD`. That entry sets NS_WORKER_CMD, which tools/port_profile.sh never reads (it reads NEURALSCREEN_MODEL_DIR and NEURALSCREEN_PORT_BIN and nothing else), so the profiler fell back to its default model; meanwhile the plain port-profile entry has had NEURALSCREEN_MODEL_DIR pointed at model-small, so the two entries' envs are swapped. The developer is correcting the policy; this run is queued so the corrected entry has something waiting for it. Read the `model:` line FIRST: it must print /opt/neuralscreen/model-small, and if it prints /opt/neuralscreen/model again the policy edit did not take and the numbers below are another repeat of the baseline. Then read the total against r2026-11-10-1-profile's 6.296 ms - that baseline is sound and is the large network, because when it ran the port-profile entry reported `env from policy: none`. Same instrument, same entry, same size as the baseline, so the pair is a clean single-variable comparison. Gate it as usual: if gpu_before reads BUSY or idle_waited_s is not 0.0, say so and do not compare. This is a re-measure rather than a retry of a dead idea - the only port sample for the small network is the October r2026-10-30-aq (26.5 ms against the large network's 24.6), taken before the port derived its stage table from the manifest, and the public reads of the 310.9.16 model call it the faster one.
